highlights.text: Motorbikes, trucks and Bren gun carriers in the cargo

summary.text: A US Army cargo ship sunk in the 1942 Darwin raid, lying about 18-19 m deep in Darwin Harbour. Its cargo of trucks and vehicles is still scattered about; tides and poor visibility make it an advanced dive.

s1.quote: It lies in 18 metres (59 ft) of water … only divable around neap tides.

hazards.text: Strong tidal currents and poor visibility; neap tides only

access.value: Exclusion zone around the wreck; permit/permission required

summary.text: A vessel lost in Cyclone Tracy in 1974 and found by divers in 2003, lying on its side in about 19-20 m in Darwin Harbour. It is a heritage site with an exclusion zone, so a permit and a boat are needed.

s1.quote: The shipwreck lies at a depth of approximately 14 metres (46 ft).
The wreck lies in 9 to 16 metres (30 to 52 ft) of water on the western side of Old Reef … requires that divers have a permit to enter the 200m protected zone

access.value: Permit required to enter the 200 m protected zone

s1.quote: St. Crispin's Reef is a popular diving and snorkeling spot for expeditions from Port Douglas and Cairns.
Flying Fish Cove is a great spot for snorkelling and shore diving … wearing reef shoes to protect your feet from sharp coral and stonefish.

s2.quote: Top: 2M Median: 9M Bottom: 25M … A very easy dive.

summary.text: A shore dive from the boat ramp in Flying Fish Cove on Christmas Island, descending a reef slope to a drop-off. It is an easy dive with rich fish and coral variety; wear reef shoes for the sharp coral and stonefish.
